## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
You should fix `test_rejects_legacy_header`: its input fails the `END` check before reaching the new version comparison, so it passes with or without this change. The production change itself matches the stated intent, and this review found no defect in it.

## Changes
The pull request tightens `parse_report` in `app/report.py` to accept only a first line exactly equal to `REPORT v1`, where it previously accepted any line starting with `REPORT `. It adds two rejection tests to `tests/test_report.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- tests/test_report.py:11 — tests — Make test_rejects_legacy_header reach the version check — The input built here is `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`: `rsplit("v1", 1)` replaces the body's `v1`, the header stays `REPORT v1`, and no `END` line exists, so `parse_report` returns `None` at `app/report.py:3`, before the version check at `app/report.py:5`. The comment on line 9 says the test works "by changing the fixture's version to v0". — The test also passes against the pre-change `startswith("REPORT ")` check, so it gives no regression protection for header-version rejection. — Fix: Give the fixture an `END` line and replace the header's version, or delete the test, because `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` already covers a `REPORT v0` header.

## Suggestions
- app/report.py:5 — tests — Add a test for a header that extends `REPORT v1` — `"REPORT v10\nvalue=ok\nEND"` now returns `None`, but no test passes a header with characters after `REPORT v1`. Loosening this line to `startswith("REPORT v1")` would keep all three tests passing. — A prefix-match regression that accepts `REPORT v10` or `REPORT v1.1` reports would go undetected.
